challenges.says: It proposes a profile before the person selects one, yet claims to honour the rule that OK does nothing until a folder is selected; the recommendation's 'explicit-choice rule still enforced' is contradicted by a preselected default.

Apart from an added preview step, it replays today's order (comments, sources, effect, remember, report) in new words, so it is barely a variant of the legacy shape, and its claim that people cannot see where changes land today is not in the legacy sentences.

The step says the same rules apply for every source kind and file encoding, but the honoured rules differ by kind (REG files fail 'not implemented' when forgetting a value, branch limits only apply to REG, POL/registry/user hive/scratch report differently), so a REG failure and the per-kind outcomes are hidden behind the recommended wording.

A check-first stage cannot say per source how the change will take effect, because the edition-dependent diff is computed from the file as last on disk at the moment of saving, and it adds a check-then-write gap the legacy 'write only if fully writable, else report not writable' rule does not have.
